newsitem.title: ROMANIA: EBRD funds breweries in Romania and Croatia.
newsitem.headline: EBRD funds breweries in Romania and Croatia.

text.p: The EBRD said on Thursday it was providing 52 million Ecus ($65 million) in loans to two breweries in Romania and Croatia to expand their production of internationally known brands.

"With the EBRD's financial support, the breweries will be able to expand production of premium local brands as well as the well-known Tuborg brand under licence," a European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) statement said.
In Romania, the London-based EBRD is lending $43 million to United Romanian Breweries Bereprod SRL, which will produce the Tuborg brand in a new brewery near Bucharest.

Construction of the brewery is to be completed by end-1997 or 1998. It is a joint venture between Carlsberg of Denmark and Israeli and Romanian partners. Its targeted output is 500,000 hectolitres a year.
Dutch Rabobank said this week it had put up $24 million to co-finance the construction of the project.
In Croatia, the EBRD is extending 33 million marks to Panoska Pivovara, for construction of a brewery in the northern part of the country.

World beer makers have rushed to Romania, Eastern Europe's largest market after Poland. Belgian, German, Turkish and Danish brewers are already in the Balkan country with an estimated $200 million in acquisitions and projects.
Romania produces about 10 million hectolitres of beer annually, with per capita consumption at only 50 litres, a third of Germany's.

With imported beers out of the reach for the average Romanian good quality beer produced locally by foreign brewers at affordable prices seems the key to boost consumption. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
